name: Street Custom 'Rebar Rose' Improvised Spike Mace
description: A length of concrete rebar bent into a handle shape with short sections of rebar welded perpendicular to the shaft, creating a crude spiked mace. The Rebar Rose is found throughout Tier 1 wherever construction salvage is available — it requires only a length of rebar, a welding arc, and the willingness to carry something that looks like a medieval weapon reimagined by an industrial accident. Despite its crude appearance, the weapon is brutally effective: the rebar spikes concentrate impact force into small areas, defeating soft armor through penetration rather than blunt force, and the heavy steel construction makes each swing potentially lethal.
specifications:
shaft length: 40-60 cm
spike count: 4-8 welded perpendicular sections
spike length: 5-10 cm
total weight: 2-4 kg depending on rebar gauge
material: Mild steel construction rebar
construction time: 30 minutes with welding equipment
concealment: Difficult — typically carried openly or in a duffel bag
story_hooks: A community defense group in Tier 1 has standardized on Rebar Rose weapons and organized patrol schedules — they are providing security where none existed, but their methods are increasingly violent.
A distinctive Rebar Rose with a specific welding pattern has been found at multiple crime scenes — the welder's signature is as unique as a fingerprint to someone who knows what to look for.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutish, utilitarian weapon that screams improvised street fabrication — a thick steel rod bent into a crude handle with perpendicular rebar spikes jutting outward like a medieval mace crossed with industrial scaffolding. No aesthetic refinement, all functional menace.
physical_description.dimensions: Shaft length: 40-60 cm (typically 50 cm), spike length: 5-10 cm protruding radially, total head width with spikes: 20-25 cm. Grip section 8-12 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Genuinely hefty and unbalanced — head-heavy, requiring commitment to swing. Feels like swinging a length of steel pipe studded with nails. Not a weapon for finesse.
physical_description.primary_material: Mild steel construction rebar — industrial-grade, unrefined
physical_description.finish: Raw mill scale and rust blooms — dark gray to brown oxidation, inconsistent surface from poor welding. Some sections show bright fresh welds, others weathered patina. No protective coating.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dark gunmetal gray with rust-brown discoloration, bright silver weld seams scattered across shaft and spike roots
physical_description.grip_texture: Bare steel, possibly wrapped with torn fabric, electrical tape, or cord for grip — rough, utilitarian, offers minimal comfort. Hand-bending marks visible in the handle curve.
distinctive_features: Asymmetrical spike placement — not precision-welded, noticeably crude
Visible weld beads — rough, unground, some with spatter
Heat discoloration rings around each weld junction — blue-gray oxidation halos
Rough cut ends on spike sections, un-dressed by grinding
Handle bend shows hammer-work marks, not precision tube bending
Possible dents and dings from test-swings or actual use
Occasional grease or construction site grime in weld valleys
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: None — this is street fabrication. Possibly spray-painted initials or gang tags on the shaft by the creator, but no official markings. Some examples may have torch-cut numbers stamped by the welder.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn and functional — this weapon is used, not maintained. Rust in weld valleys, splatter patterns from multiple fabrication attempts, possible bent spikes from impact, handle wrap deteriorating from sweat and grime. Each example is unique in its wear.

Dark dramatic side-lighting reveals rough weld seams and rust blooms, casting sharp shadows from the jutting spikes. Shallow depth of field focuses on weld detail.
